data.statement: Distinction is not equivalent to RT; RT status is acquired through relational participation rather than mere existence.
Residue actively deforms topology and prevents exact collapse, driving emergence of history-conditioned continuation.
The primary controllable variable is the evaluation process architecture rather than the identity of operands; Governance is a first-class process component.

Adversarial hardening enters the Mono-Process repository as governance infrastructure before theory backfill patches, and all downstream backfills in the series remain sequenced under explicit ontology leakage, meta-level, whole-expression, array-classification, residue-inscription, and implementation-firewall review.

Whole Expression Primacy dictates that an RT expression is the minimum indivisible unit of analysis, preventing modular ablation, state-first, node-first, or component-first readings, and defining structural aspect decomposition as purely analytical projection.

Affect and Effect are inseparable, co-generative process aspect-positions of the mono-process within the RT/Core expression, where Affect establishes the continuous tension/necessity aspect and Effect represents discrete realization, neither possessing ontological priority or substrate primitivity.

Dual Inscription dictates that residue update events are partitioned into realized continuation inscription (Psi_plus) and excluded boundary inscription (Psi_minus), preventing any hidden-state ontology drift and ensuring both active updates and boundary exclusions constrain future admissibility.

The Abstraction Meta-Level Stack stratifies process arguments into eight levels (Projection, Realization, Arbitration, Admissibility, Relation, Participation, Evaluation, and RT/Core), mandating explicit declaration of level scope for critiques, patches, and proofs to prevent illicit layer movement.

Array Classification Requirement mandates that all arrays in formalisms and simulations declare their type (conditional, projection, residue, or participation), strictly banning generic state arrays to prevent snapshot/substance ontology leakage under recursive updates.

Closure Neighborhoods Requirement mandates that all process coupling neighborhoods (or closure neighborhoods) be defined and computed strictly via local process-connectivity relations (such as mutual admissibility window overlap or explicit orientation-array topology crossings) rather than assuming a primitive spatial coordinate metric or persistent node objects.

Topology-to-Geometry Legality Transform (Pi_geo) defines a projection condition under which a stabilized topological organization may be represented as geometry_app without treating geometry as primitive, provided it preserves distinction class, admissibility status, orientation traceability, and closure traceability as defined in L099 and L100.

Within these models, a Projection Signature (Sig_app) is represented as a recognizable pattern of constraints, outputs, and preserved relations showing that a process expression has lawfully projected into an application-facing domain.

Within these models, same-direction RT forms collapse locally, but opposite typed collapse residues (0_minus and 0_plus) may participate in higher-order RT and become admissible under a declared higher-order comparison, provided they retain directional provenance and are not reduced to undifferentiated zero.

Within these models, X is RT iff X constructively traces its dependency lineage to RT_core without breaking distinction, admissibility, residue closure, or non-collapse. RT formation is computationally defined as [delta_a(B_L) <*>_x delta_a(B_R)], requiring distinction-bearing generative paths, block admissibility, polarity preservation, and non-identity between blocks.

Within these models, Constraint Geometry is represented as the triangular knot-closure △(RT, QM_app, GR_app), geometrically restating the Core co-generative structure and providing a triadic bridge where grammar and projections remain distinguishable inside one lawful closure.
